novel_features.name: Change digest
novel_features.description: See new listings, price drops, and status flips since a prior sync — a Saturday-morning scan of the whole catalog.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local snapshot history across syncs; the WordPress API serves only current state.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when someone asks what is new or changed instead of re-reading all 84 cards.

novel_features.name: Price-per-acre leaderboard
novel_features.description: Rank budget-filtered listings by price per acre, cheapest first.
novel_features.rationale: Computes price divided by acres across the mirror; the site shows the two figures separately and never divides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it when a user cares about land value per acre, not asking price alone.

novel_features.name: Side-by-side compare
novel_features.description: Aligned feature table for 2-4 named listings in one call.
novel_features.rationale: One local join replaces several show round-trips and emits an aligned comparison no single API call provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it when the user names a specific set of listings to weigh against each other.

novel_features.name: Comparables with deltas
novel_features.description: Nearest peer listings for one property, with price and per-acre deltas; sold comps opt-in.
novel_features.rationale: Local peer scoring over stored fields; the site's similar-listings grid is editorial and carries no numbers.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it before pricing or offers to ground one property against its market.

novel_features.name: District market report
novel_features.description: Counts, median price, median price per acre, and status mix for a district and its towns.
novel_features.rationale: Percentile statistics plus the synced district/child-town hierarchy; no WordPress endpoint aggregates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for regional summaries before drilling into individual listings.

novel_features.name: Mirror coverage report
novel_features.description: Per-field fill rates across mirrored listings so operators know which answers the mirror can currently support.
novel_features.rationale: COUNT-based audit over scraped columns surfaces exactly which captured fields are missing.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run it after a sync to know which questions the local mirror can answer today.

narrative.headline: All 84 Ceiba listings offline, with market math, comps, and change tracking over a local mirror.
narrative.value_prop: ceiba-cli mirrors the full Ceiba Realty catalog — land, farms, homes, islands and developments — into local SQLite, then answers with structured one-call commands: filtered search, complete detail payloads, price-per-acre rankings, district market reports, comparables, and what-changed digests. Sold listings stay hidden by default, and payloads carry their source (live or local) plus freshness metadata where the mirror tracks it.

quickstart.comment: Verify the CLI installs and the Ceiba source is reachable before fetching anything.
Mirror all 84 listings, districts, developments, and media metadata into local SQLite.
Budget-filtered search across the mirror; sold listings stay hidden by default.
One complete payload: USD/BZD pricing, specs, gallery, map, brochure, and similar listings.
Rank budget listings by price per acre — math the website never shows.

troubleshoots.fix: Run ceiba-cli-pp-cli doctor — the site's ModSecurity gate requires browser-like headers; doctor reports when the block resurfaces.

troubleshoots.symptom: Search returns nothing after a first run
troubleshoots.fix: Run ceiba-cli-pp-cli sync --full to rebuild the mirror, then re-run the search.

troubleshoots.symptom: An expected sold listing never appears
troubleshoots.fix: Sold listings are hidden by design; add --include-sold to the search.

troubleshoots.symptom: Fields like map coordinates or listing IDs are empty for some listings
troubleshoots.fix: Run ceiba-cli-pp-cli coverage to see fill rates; the site itself omits these on some listings.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI whenever the task is about Belize property inventory from Ceiba Realty: finding listings by budget, acreage, district or lifestyle; answering detailed questions about a specific property; comparing candidates; sizing up comps; or catching up on what changed. It is the right tool for chat assistants and agents that need structured answers without scraping Elementor pages. Commands answer from the local mirror, so run `sync` after install and again later — `changes` needs at least two syncs to report what moved.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to submit interest, contact, or preferences forms — it is read-only and stores no PII.
Do not use it to download or cache images; it returns absolute URLs for hot-linking.
Do not use it for blogs, region guides, giveaways, or property-map geo-bounds queries — out of scope in v0.1.
Do not use it as a general WordPress admin client; only the public Ceiba listing surfaces are modeled.
